ingredients.note: halved from 1/4 tsp for low heat

meals.notes: Loved redo (5 stars, Oct). Pool day: brown the chicken, build the saffron-fennel broth, nestle the thighs on the potatoes skin-up, oven 375°F, then broil to crisp; cool and refrigerate. At dinner reheat covered at 350°F and broil a few minutes to re-crisp the skin. 6 servings: Sun + Mon dinners for two, his Mon + Tue lunches. Seafood-free despite the name. Skim the fat (heart-health). Monday dinner is the leftovers: reheat covered at 350°F, broil to re-crisp; fresh garlic toasts. Lower-sodium build (2026-11-21): 3/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher in total, no-salt-added tomatoes; lean on the saffron, orange zest, pastis and a squeeze of lemon at the table. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

ingredients.note: canned, drained and rinsed (regular canned, rinsed, adds about 50 mg per pepper)

meals.notes: One-dish full meal (beef, rice, peppers), dairy-free. Soak the rice 20-30 min while you chop. Brown onion then beef deeply; add parsley, rice, paprika, tomato sauce + 2 1/4 cups water, simmer to half, then low and covered 20 min. Meanwhile char the peppers on a grill pan or skillet 10-15 min, covered, turning. Stuff, set in a dish with 3/4 cup broth/water, foil-tent, 350°F for 20-30 min. 6 peppers: Tue dinner for two, his Wed lunch, Wed dinner for two, 1 to freeze for a lunch. Freezes 1-2 months; reheat in a medium oven with a splash of liquid. Red meat night of the week (1/2 lb across 6 = lean). Wednesday dinner is the leftovers: reheat covered at 350°F with a splash of water, ~20 min. Lower-sodium build (2026-11-21): 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher in total, no-salt-added tomato sauce and chickpeas, water in the baking dish; finish with lemon. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

meals.title: Grilled Duck Breasts in Cherry-Port Sauce
meals.source: Meathead: The Science of Great Barbecue and Grilling — p.315

ingredients.note: "plump" (book: 2 breasts = 2 servings; 1 per person). Hard to find: Whole Foods / Bristol Farms / Gelson's, or frozen at Asian markets
dried sage, parsley, rosemary, thyme, oregano, basil, bay, black pepper, sugar, pulsed coarse; make a pinch-batch at home
2 for the shallots, 2 to mount the sauce
book: balsamic (or raspberry vinegar); his menu uses red wine vinegar
book: dried cherries; sour per his menu. Alt: dried cranberries or raisins (book notes)
a few sprigs in the sauce, per his menu (not in the book recipe)
dry brine for both breasts (about 1 lb): Meathead's 1/2 tsp per pound

meals.notes: Scaled for 2 (book makes 2). Score the skin in a 3/4-1 in crosshatch through the fat, salt + rub both sides, dry brine ~3 hr. Book method: two-zone grill, cast-iron pan preheated on the hot side 10 min; skin side down until dark brown, flip and sear 3 min, move breasts to the indirect side to 135°F (~30 min). Sauce in the wiped pan: 2 tbsp butter, shallots till limp, then broth, port, vinegar and cherries reduced by half; mount with 2 tbsp butter. Slice thin on an angle, fan over sauce. No grill at the rental: render skin-side down over medium in cast iron (pour off fat as it builds), flip and sear 3 min, finish in a 300–325°F oven to 135°F; vent the kitchen, it smokes. Save the clean duck fat for potatoes.

meals.title: Pear Tarte Tatin

ingredients.note: firm, slightly underripe; halve and pack in as many as fit the 10-in skillet (they shrink). FN calls for 12-15 underripe Anjou
10-11 in; larger than the pan. Dufour (Whole Foods) or Trader Joe's seasonal all-butter
his menu adds butter to the caramel; stir in off the heat once it turns golden (not in the FN recipe)

meals.notes: FN method: 400°F. CLEAN 10-in cast-iron skillet; 3/4 cup sugar + 3 tbsp water over medium-low, swirl, don't stir, until golden, 10-12 min. Off heat, pack in the pear halves (crowd them; they shrink). Back on low ~20 min until the fruit soaks up the caramel. Drape the puff pastry over, tuck the edges, cut three 2-in slits. Bake 40-45 min until browned and the pears are tender. Cool only 10-15 min, pour off and reserve excess caramel, flip onto a platter, pour the caramel back, push loose fruit into place. Serve with vanilla ice cream. (Skipping the recipe's optional cranberry caramel.) Tips: firm, slightly underripe pears; clean utensils or the caramel goes grainy. Bake it in the cast-iron skillet he's bringing. It serves 8–10, so there's tart for Friday breakfast too.

assumptions: about 75% of a 14 oz all-butter puff pastry sheet is used after trimming
